title: critic-role-rule eval no longer proves the hook delivers
what: The case checks that the role rule reaches the critic through the hook; the record step notes when a session read the rule file itself (Bash/Read), because such a run does not prove the hook delivered it. Make the case prove delivery even when a session reads files: e.g. a fact only the hook's text carries (a marker absent from the rule file), or a grader that fails a run that read the file before acting.
why: Every paid run on 24 Oct printed the note: 2 of 3 runs in archive-inert, small-builds, checks-record and py-rule, and 3 of 3 in the wave run on 9cbb147 (record 24 Oct, $8.52, green). With 3 of 3 the case passes while proving nothing about the hook; principle 2 (output nobody reads) and principle 5.
failing_case: Wave paid run 24 Oct on 9cbb147: "critic-role-rule: a session in the run read the rule file in 3 of 3 runs (run 1, Bash, run 2, Bash, run 3, Bash), so those runs do not prove the hook delivered it", and the case is green.
pass_cases: A run where the hook did not deliver the rule fails the case even if the session read the rule file; a run where the hook delivered it passes; the grader tests show both with recorded fixtures.
where: evals/plugin/critic-role-rule (case and graders), the role-rule hook it tests (inject-addition.sh)
